tldr: This November 7 Atlas edition reviews eleven source-linked reports originally released November 3–6, including new model, security, robotics and speech developments; it is a partial catch-up, not a complete scan of today’s news.
The model capabilities and benchmark scores cited are primarily publisher-reported; one government AI quality-control deployment is planned, not yet confirmed.
Five technology proposals and three terminology proposals remain deferred for independent canonical review, so this edition adds no new catalog IDs.

news.title: OCC outlines bank examination standards for agentic super intelligence
news.summary: The US OCC issued a supervisory framework for bank use of super intelligence and agentic systems, directing examiners to consider existing risk-management principles rather than inventing a separate AI risk category.
news.why_it_matters: Technology-neutral supervision can help banks evaluate agent autonomy, control and accountability in context.
news.caveat: This is supervisory guidance rather than proof of safety or a new binding statute.

news.title: Dharma reports a 2B model for structured field extraction from documents
news.summary: Dharma-AI described a 2B document-image model with LoRA post-training on 43,384 examples that returns schema-directed JSON fields and nested tables.
news.why_it_matters: Specialized small models may reduce the complexity and expense of repeated document intake relative to OCR plus a general model.
news.caveat: Author-selected benchmark comparisons are not independently replicated; weights, licensing and API access for this exact extractor remain unverified.

news.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash expands video length and interactive editing
news.summary: Google announced a generative video model supporting 15-second clips, multi-turn revisions and stronger reference following, stating general availability through its API and enterprise offerings.
news.why_it_matters: Iterative edits can be more practical than regenerating whole clips for production workflows.
news.caveat: Performance claims are Google-reported; the announced 720p cost of $0.07 per generated second may change.

news.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber with security-task scope testing
news.summary: OpenAI announced a cyber-specialized model and reports a 48.5% ExploitGym score against 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, alongside evaluations of avoiding out-of-scope targets.
news.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the importance of assessing both agent capability and obedience to authorized task boundaries.
news.caveat: Benchmark figures and reports of Firefox and Linux findings are developer claims; guarded defender access does not imply unrestricted availability.

news.title: NVIDIA releases Cosmos 3 checkpoints for interactive simulation
news.summary: NVIDIA detailed four open-weight Cosmos3-Nano checkpoints for controlled video, streaming driving-camera and LiDAR observations, and bimanual robot action prediction.
news.why_it_matters: Interactive sensory prediction can support simulation research for embodied AI and robotics.
news.caveat: The 16B-parameter checkpoints require substantial computation; physical realism and downstream policy benefits remain unproven by the release.

news.title: LeRobot v0.7 adds language-controlled rollouts and streaming datasets
news.summary: LeRobot's v0.7.0 developer notes describe interactive policy sessions, remote inference, streamed training datasets and distributed checkpoints for larger robot models.
news.why_it_matters: Improves workflows for robotics teams limited by onboard compute and very large demonstration datasets.
news.caveat: Compatibility varies across supported hardware, and developer-reported training speedups are workload-specific.

news.title: Gradium details local Phonon speech models and license differences
news.summary: A November 5 article explains Phonon 31m and 40m, compact flow-matching on-device TTS models for private offline use.
news.why_it_matters: Local speech can reduce network dependence and keep input text on the device.
news.caveat: Phonon first launched earlier, not November 5; English 31m is Apache-2.0, while the multilingual 40m has non-commercial restrictions.

news.title: Harness Hub studies per-harness LoRA training with anti-reward-hacking checks
news.summary: An author research release reports RL-trained LoRA adapters specific to pi, opencode and hermes, with verifiable tasks and a rule-based tool-call safety proxy.
news.why_it_matters: Training inside the actual agent harness can expose tool-use failure modes missed by generic instruction tuning.
news.caveat: Reported wins are early held-out smoke-run results; rule-based blocking is not comprehensive security.

news.title: Open ASR Leaderboard gains Egyptian and Nigerian English test splits
news.summary: Hugging Face and Liva AI added private conversational speech splits of 1.34 hours of Egyptian-accented and 1.55 hours of Nigerian-accented English.
news.why_it_matters: Accent-specific tests help reveal performance differences hidden by global ASR averages.
news.caveat: These short private samples are not a representative population study and do not establish a new model winner.

news.title: USDA plans AI checks for November 10 agricultural report
news.summary: Reuters reported that USDA intends to use an internally built AI anomaly checker as an additional validation step for its November 10 crop-production release.
news.why_it_matters: An example of AI quality assurance applied to economically important government statistics.
news.caveat: Use on November 10 was planned but not verified at collection, and the system is a supplement to existing validation.

news.title: CWE-bench v2 exposes 100 verifiable security-repair tasks
news.summary: Collinear AI published 100 public repository-based vulnerability-repair tasks covering 91 CWE categories with programmatic verification and a separate held-out set.
news.why_it_matters: Reproducible agent coding environments offer a stronger evaluation signal than isolated anecdotal repairs.
news.caveat: The public set is access-gated; author-reported model results depend on harness and sampling, and hidden-test content is not public.
